video_title: Will Hardy talks about Utah’s fight in the fourth, Collier’s contributions vs Miami

quotes.speaker: Will Hardy
quotes.summary_phrase: Will Hardy on Simone Fontecchio's fourth-quarter shooting performance
quotes.excerpt: I think the emotion of the moment, it was obviously a big moment for our team.
quotes.quote: You saw Simone Fontecchio's reaction. I think the emotion of the moment, it was obviously a big moment for our team. Our fans were incredible tonight, but I think you can see the emotion that Simone plays with and shows, how much it means to him. Simone has had some things not go his way personally lately, and he's been an incredible teammate. He's worked really hard. He's not had one moment of complaining. It's amazing when you just kind of give yourself to the team, the good things can happen, but I'm happy for Simone.
quotes.social_post: Will Hardy praised Simone Fontecchio for his emotional resilience and team-first attitude after a tough stretch personally. It is amazing when you just give yourself to the team, the good things can happen.

structured.context: Will Hardy discusses Simone Fontecchio's emotional performance and his attitude as a teammate during a recent game.

quotes.speaker: Will Hardy
quotes.summary_phrase: Will Hardy on Keyonte George and Ochai Agbaji's offensive poise
quotes.excerpt: They're playing with poise. They're just taking the game as it comes at them.
quotes.quote: They're playing with poise. They're just taking the game as it comes at them. They don't feel like they're forcing it. I think Keyonte George in the fourth quarter had a few possessions where he overdribbled and got a little too low on the court when he picked his dribble up, but it's my job to coach him and nitpick some of those things. But I think in general, both of those guys are showing a ton of poise for where they are in their careers. You're watching their understanding grow because they're doing it within the construct of the team.
quotes.social_post: Will Hardy says Keyonte George and Ochai Agbaji are showing a ton of poise for where they are in their careers. He noted that both players are growing by playing within the construct of the team.

structured.context: Will Hardy evaluates the offensive poise and development of young players Keyonte George and Ochai Agbaji.

quotes.speaker: Will Hardy
quotes.summary_phrase: Will Hardy on diagnosing turnovers and team rotation adjustments
quotes.excerpt: I think it's just the types of turnovers. Not all turnovers are the same.
quotes.quote: I think it's just the types of turnovers. Not all turnovers are the same. We have 19 of them, only eight are live ball, so you're looking at things like moving screens or the ball going out of bounds, whether that's off the dribble, a pass. Like Simone through that rocket there towards the end, that was a great look, just missed Josh Green. So I think we always go back and watch and we have to evaluate, is this a decision-making turnover, like we made a bad choice, or is it a physical error, like I tried to pass to you, you were the right person to pass to, and I just threw it too high.
quotes.social_post: Will Hardy on the Jazz turnover issues. He says not all turnovers are the same and they evaluate whether they are decision making errors or physical mistakes.

structured.context: Will Hardy explains his process for analyzing and categorizing team turnovers after a game.

quotes.speaker: Will Hardy
quotes.summary_phrase: Will Hardy on Kris Dunn's development as a primary ball-handler
quotes.excerpt: I think he's handling ball pressure really well. That's the biggest thing that I'm seeing.
quotes.quote: I think he's handling ball pressure really well. That's the biggest thing that I'm seeing. In back-to-back games, like when he's the primary handler, last game with Jaden McDaniels picking him up, and then a guy like Davion Mitchell, who has a big-time reputation in our league for ball pressure, I think Kris Dunn is handling himself pretty well. Using his burst, better at setting up screens, being more patient, and then he's starting to really see the moments when the ball has to be kicked to his teammates to allow the game to open up for him as it goes along. Being a primary decision-maker is hard, but Kris Dunn's studying it a lot, he's working on it a ton, and I think we're seeing a ton of growth.
quotes.social_post: Will Hardy is seeing growth in Kris Dunn as a primary ball handler. He says Dunn is handling ball pressure well and learning to see the moments when the ball has to be kicked to his teammates.

structured.context: Will Hardy praises Kris Dunn for his growth and ability to handle ball pressure against defensive specialists.
